_comment: Enrollment manifest for the CI test gates. Every workspace that pnpm-workspace.yaml
resolves must appear here — either with a floor under `vitest.workspaces`, or with a
written reason under `vitest.exempt`. A workspace that exists on disk and is missing
from both fails the gate, so adding a package without adding tests is a red build
rather than a global count that silently absorbs the gap.
Floors are per project, not global: a package that stops contributing tests entirely
cannot hide behind its neighbours' counts. Raising a floor is a normal part of adding
tests; lowering one is a decision that shows up in review — see `ratchet` below, and
scripts/ci/assert-floor-ratchet.mjs, which compares every number here against the same
file on origin/main.
Floors sit a little under the real counts on purpose. They are a loss detector, not a
target: the point is to catch a suite that shrank, not to go red every time a test is
renamed away.
ORIGIN OF THIS FILE ON THIS BRANCH (#26 auth, round 6). The gate scripts and the
workflow live on `fix/ci-r6`, not here and not yet on main; this file is that branch's
manifest with the two workspaces #26 created enrolled into it. It is here rather than
left for whoever merges because the branch that adds a workspace is the branch that
knows what its floor should be, and because `assert-workspace-enrollment.mjs` fails on
a workspace that is present and undeclared — which, on the merged tree, `packages/auth`
and the new `apps/web` Vitest project both are. Both branches add this path, so the
merge is a conflict on one file: take this version, it is the superset.
Counted from a real run of this branch (pnpm test: 637 tests, 30 files):
core 129, db 23, auth 219, ingest 150, server 104, web 12.
Floors ratchet up. scripts/ci/assert-floor-ratchet.mjs reads this same file from
origin/main and fails if any floor here is lower than the one there — including the
quiet version, where an enrolled workspace is moved into `exempt` instead.
A decrease is allowed with a written reason keyed to exactly what came down, e.g.
"vitest.workspaces.packages/core.minTests": "why the suite is legitimately smaller".
Justifications are checked in both directions: one that does not match an actual
decrease fails too, so nobody can pre-authorise next month's cut by landing a blanket
reason today.
There is no baseline until a manifest merges — origin/main carries none yet — so
today the script says `no baseline` loudly and checks only that every floor is a
whole number of at least 1. It becomes a real ratchet the moment a manifest exists on
main.
`apps/web` moved out of `exempt` and into `workspaces` this round. That direction is
a tightening and needs no justification: the exemption said the workspace stayed
browser-free and contributed zero unit tests by design, and round 5 gave it a Vitest
project because `lib/env.ts` — the file that decides whether the app serves
production traffic — had had no unit test for four rounds. The exemption's stated
reason stopped being true, and `assert-vitest-report.mjs` fails a project that runs
while unenrolled, so leaving it exempt would have been red rather than quiet.
Other workspaces' floors are left exactly as `fix/ci-r6` calibrated them, even where
this branch's counts are far above them (db 23 vs 10, server 104 vs 22). Raising
somebody else's floor from a branch they cannot see is how a ratchet ends up encoding
one branch's tree as everyone's minimum. `minTotalTests` is the one shared number
that had to move — 300 would be a loss detector that never fires against 637.
